Buying guide · Size

Condom size chart: read the width and you know it fits

The nominal width on the box is the one number that decides whether a condom fits. It is half your erect circumference, so a width of 52 mm means a circumference of about 10.4 cm. Read that one number and there is nothing left to guess.

Last updated 2026-11-05

On this page
  1. First: measure yourself, once
  2. The common sizes, side by side
  3. Between two sizes: take the wider one
  4. Which of the four T-ZERO styles is yours?

First: measure yourself, once

Take a soft measuring tape, or a strip of paper and a pen. While fully erect, measure around the base of the penis, where it is widest. Let the tape rest against the skin without squeezing it, because squeezing gives you a smaller number than the real one.

Divide the circumference in centimetres by two and you have your width in millimetres. A circumference of 10.5 cm gives a width of 52.5 mm, so look for the size marked "52 ± 2 mm".

How to measure without it being awkward

Do it at home, after a shower, with a soft tape. Nobody sees it, nothing has to be pressed or squeezed, and it is not uncomfortable. Once a year is enough.

The common sizes, side by side

Width (mm) Circumference Common label Who it suits
44 ± 2 about 8.8 cm S / Small Narrower build, or you like a close fit
49 ± 2 about 9.8 cm M / Medium The standard size most people wear
54 ± 2 about 10.8 cm L / Large You want less tension, or M feels tight
58 ± 2 about 11.6 cm XL / Extra large L still feels tight
62 ± 2 about 12.4 cm XXL / Extra extra large You want more room and less restraint

Condoms sold in Hong Kong usually print the width on the box, such as "52±2", while some brands print only S / M / L. When the width is printed, use the width, because one "S" can be 44 mm and another 47 mm.

Between two sizes: take the wider one

If you land exactly between two sizes, take the wider one. Too narrow constricts, which reduces blood flow and can make things soften, and it is uncomfortable. Too wide simply slips.

  • A good fit stays on, does not pinch, and does not slip.
  • Leave a little space at the tip, about the width of a fingertip, so there is somewhere for the small amount of fluid that comes with an erection.
  • If it feels right but slightly loose, that is the right size. Do not change it.

Which of the four T-ZERO styles is yours?

All four T-ZERO NINTH SENSE styles come in the same width family; what differs is the film and the finish. Ultra Thin is the thinnest and the least noticeable. Extra Lube carries the most lubricant, for anyone who tends to run dry. Extended is a thicker, sturdier film. Studded has raised texture.

All four are available at Watsons and HKTVmall. If you are unsure of your size, message us on WhatsApp, or start with a box of three and try.

Frequently asked questions

What does "52±2 mm" on the box actually mean?

52 mm is the nominal width, and ±2 mm is the tolerance, so the real width may be anywhere from 50 to 54 mm. Width is half the erect circumference, so 52 mm means a circumference of roughly 10.4 cm.

I cannot measure. Can I estimate from my height?

Not reliably. Height and penile size are only weakly related, so a height-based estimate is usually wrong. The tape takes a minute and is far more accurate.

Is a larger size safer?

No. Every genuine condom has to pass ISO 4071, which covers burst pressure, tensile strength and an electrical test on every single condom. Width has nothing to do with safety; it is about comfort and staying on.
